co_turkey_rocks.blurb: Turkey Rocks is a group of rock formations in the South Platte area of Colorado, near Woodland Park at about 8,240 feet. It is a crack climber's place: nearly everything is traditional, with a handful of top-rope, sport and bouldering lines mixed in. Grades run from about 5.6 to 5.12, with the bulk between 5.8 and 5.11 and only a few at the top end. The crags face generally south, and winter climbing is often possible. The south face of Turkey Rock holds most of the multi-pitch classics, Turkey Perch is the spot for popular single-pitch 5.7 and 5.8 climbs, and Turkey Tail has the harder lines. Leftovers and Rightovers round out the five formations.

md_cumberland_narrows_aka_lover_s_leap.blurb: The Narrows is a water gap just west of the city of Cumberland in western Maryland, where Wills Creek cuts between Wills Mountain and Haystack Mountain, both capped by Tuscarora quartzite. The cliff above the city runs for about a mile and reaches up to roughly 200 feet. Trad and top-rope climbing split the routes almost evenly, and bolts are rare, so expect to build anchors from trees; finding your way through thick foliage is part of the day. Grades are mostly 5.6 to 5.10, with some easier routes and a few multipitch lines. The cliff faces southwest and catches afternoon sun, which is pleasant much of the year and very hot in summer. Cumber Honey Wall, Funland and Howling Wall lead the trad, and a string of top-rope buttresses sits alongside.

or_terra_nova.blurb: Terra Nova is a sport-climbing area in Southwest Oregon, laid out as a series of walls and alcoves rather than one big cliff. Every climb is bolted, mostly 5.10 and 5.11 with a good number at 5.12 and a smaller group of 5.7 to 5.9 routes to warm up on. Named sections include the Bone Yard, 1st Alcove, Emerald City, Valhalla and Rock City Wall. At Rock City Wall the routes mix 5.10 and 5.11 with a few harder ones, and the upper headwall adds longer extension pitches. The Bone Yard Alcove is compact and single-pitch and faces west, so plan on afternoon sun there; spring and fall suit it best.

az_priest_draw.blurb: Priest Draw is a bouldering area south of Flagstaff in northern Arizona, a few miles south of The Ridge. The rock is limestone, and the draw is best known for pocketed roof problems, a style that can feel unfamiliar at first. Many problems sit under the roofs, so the rock stays dry and sheltered and the area can be climbed nearly year-round. Grades cover everything from V0 to V13, with plenty of problems at V0 to V5 and a solid hard tier above V8. Well-known formations include Welcome Boulder, Puzzle Box, Monster Roof, Anorexic Roof, Bat Roof and Mars Roof.

ma_stone_tower_area.blurb: Stone Tower Area sits in Lynn Woods, a municipal forest on the North Shore of Massachusetts about ten miles north of Boston. The woods are scattered with glacial erratics and surrounded by several large reservoirs, and the boulders across the woods are mostly coarse-grained granite. Everything here is bouldering, from V0 up to V9, with most problems between V0 and V6. The centerpiece is the Stone Tower Boulder, a house-sized block with problems on every side, and nearby groups include the Gem Boulders, Gully Boulders and Queen's Row Boulders. Across Lynn Woods, walks to the boulders run from a few minutes to over half an hour.
